summary: Buta territory (Bas-Uele) is far from the active conflict zones of eastern DRC and no armed group is reported to hold territory there as of late 2025-2026. Buta, the provincial capital, is administered and policed by the state: PNC conducts routine policing and arrests (e.g. the November 2025 police raid on Radio Liberte Buta), with a thin FARDC garrison that local actors in early 2026 described as understrength. Rural Buta secteur and the Titule area along the Buta-Titule-Isiro road/rail axis have no reported armed-group control; insecurity there is limited to banditry, poaching and occasional herder-farmer tensions. All locations are assigned to state control (PNC) by default state presence.

sources.title: Police close radio station, detain radio technician in northern DRC
Agression rwandaise: Obed Mutuale appelle a renforcer les FARDC dans le Bas-Uele

zones.description: Buta town (provincial capital of Bas-Uele), all neighbourhoods
zones.evidence: Buta is the seat of Bas-Uele provincial institutions; PNC performs routine policing and arrests (police raid and arrest at Radio Liberte Buta, Nov 2025). FARDC garrison present but reportedly understrength in early 2026; no armed-group activity reported.

zones.description: Rural Buta secteur villages near Buta (Mabenge, Gwa, Bale, Sukisa)
zones.evidence: No armed-group presence reported in Buta health zone; state administration from nearby Buta town. Sparse police/administrative presence assumed by default.

zones.description: Titule health zone (Titule/Kpondolia, Gbulusu, Mabinza, Gare 4, Mokpanga, Liguga)
zones.evidence: No reports of armed-group control in Titule area in 2025-2026; Bas-Uele security forces described as thin, so state presence is weak but uncontested. Assigned to PNC by default.
